name: Sample: the Bill of Rights
notes:
The Bill of Rights:
1st Amendment: freedom of speech, religion and the press.
2nd Amendment: the right to bear arms.
3rd Amendment: soldiers can't be housed in your home.
4th Amendment: no searches without a warrant.
5th Amendment: you can stay silent instead of testifying against yourself.
6th Amendment: a speedy trial with a lawyer.
7th Amendment: a jury trial in civil lawsuits.
8th Amendment: no cruel or unusual punishment.
9th Amendment: rights not listed still belong to the people.
10th Amendment: powers not given to the federal government belong to the states.

stops.label: tv screen
stops.fact: The 1st Amendment protects freedom of speech, religion and the press.
stops.scene: A giant hamburger BUN reads the news on the TV: it SPEAKS into a mic, a choir PRAYS behind it, and newspapers PRINT out of the screen.
stops.hook: 1 → bun · speech, religion, press → a mic, a choir, a printing press
stops.imagePrompt: A cheerful hamburger bun news anchor on a TV screen holding a microphone, a small choir singing behind it, newspapers flying out of the screen

stops.label: chess set
stops.fact: The 2nd Amendment grants the right to bear arms.
stops.scene: A grizzly BEAR in giant SHOES sits at the chess set, flexing two huge hairy ARMS, and sweeps every chess piece off the board.
stops.hook: 2 → shoe · bear arms → a BEAR with huge ARMS
stops.imagePrompt: A grizzly bear wearing giant sneakers sitting at a giant chess board, flexing huge muscular arms, chess pieces flying off the board

stops.label: foosball table
stops.fact: The 3rd Amendment prohibits soldiers from being housed in private homes.
stops.scene: The foosball players are tiny SOLDIERS trying to move into your HOUSE. A TREE grows through the table and flicks them out, one by one: not in my home!
stops.imagePrompt: A foosball table whose little players are toy soldiers carrying suitcases toward a tiny house, a tree growing through the table flicking them away

stops.label: glass doors
stops.fact: The 4th Amendment protects against searches without a warrant.
stops.scene: Police knock on the glass DOORS to SEARCH the Reitz. You hold the door shut until they press a WARRANT to the glass: no warrant, no search.
stops.hook: 4 → door · search → police at the door · warrant → the paper on the glass
stops.imagePrompt: Two police officers at tall glass doors holding magnifying glasses, a person inside holding the door shut, a big paper warrant pressed against the glass

stops.label: gator statue
stops.fact: The 5th Amendment allows individuals to remain silent instead of testifying against themselves.
stops.scene: A HIVE of bees buzzes around the gator statue asking questions, but the gator SNAPS its jaws shut and won't say a word. It pleads the Fifth.
stops.hook: 5 → hive · stay silent → the gator's jaws snapped shut
stops.imagePrompt: A bronze alligator statue with its jaws clamped shut and a zipper over its mouth, a buzzing beehive with bees holding tiny microphones around it

stops.label: staircase
stops.fact: The 6th Amendment guarantees a speedy trial with a lawyer.
stops.scene: A LAWYER in a suit sprints up the staircase on six wooden STICKS for stilts, waving a stopwatch and yelling 'SPEEDY TRIAL!'
stops.hook: 6 → sticks · speedy trial → a lawyer racing a stopwatch
stops.imagePrompt: A lawyer in a suit with a briefcase sprinting up a staircase on stilts made of wooden sticks, holding a stopwatch, speed lines

stops.label: orange chairs
stops.fact: The 7th Amendment guarantees a jury trial in civil lawsuits.
stops.scene: Twelve ANGELS float down into the rows of orange chairs: they're the JURY. On the big screen, two neighbors sue each other over a lawnmower: a CIVIL lawsuit.
stops.hook: 7 → heaven (angels) · jury → angels in the jury chairs · civil → neighbors suing
stops.imagePrompt: Angels with halos sitting in rows of orange armchairs like a jury box, watching a big screen showing two neighbors arguing over a lawnmower

stops.label: barbershop
stops.fact: The 8th Amendment prohibits cruel or unusual punishment.
stops.scene: In the barbershop, a barber gives a CRUEL and UNUSUAL haircut: half mohawk, half bowl cut. A GATE slams down over the door: that punishment is banned!
stops.hook: 8 → gate · cruel and unusual punishment → a cruel, unusual haircut
stops.imagePrompt: A barbershop with a barber giving a customer a ridiculous half-mohawk half-bowl-cut haircut, a metal gate slamming down in front of the shop

stops.label: vending machine
stops.fact: The 9th Amendment states that rights not listed still belong to the people.
stops.scene: The vending machine sells WINE that isn't on its menu. The label says 'not listed', but the PEOPLE in line take it anyway: it still belongs to them.
stops.hook: 9 → wine · rights not listed → things not on the menu
stops.imagePrompt: A snack vending machine with bottles of wine in a slot labeled 'not listed', a happy line of people taking them

stops.label: elevator
stops.fact: The 10th Amendment states that powers not given to the federal government belong to the states.
stops.scene: A superHERO eating a BUN rides the elevator. It skips the 'FEDERAL' floor and opens on 'THE STATES', where he hands out glowing POWER buttons.
stops.hook: 10 → bun + hero · powers → the elevator's buttons, given to the states
stops.imagePrompt: A superhero eating a hamburger bun inside an elevator, the button for a 'Federal' floor crossed out, handing glowing power buttons to people waving state flags
